SCADA Abaran · Odoo Integration Help

Type: SQL Database Connection (pyodbc)

1) Database Connection

Uses pyodbc library to connect to legacy SCADA SQL Server databases.

Connection Parameters (JSON):

{
  "driver_name": "FreeTDS",
  "host": "192.168.1.100",
  "port": 1433,
  "database": "scada_abaran_db",
  "user": "scada_user",
  "password": "password",
  "tds_version": "7.0"
}

Common driver names:

  • "SQL Server" - Modern SQL Server (2012+)
  • "FreeTDS" - Legacy SQL Server or Linux environments
  • "ODBC Driver 17 for SQL Server" - Latest Microsoft driver

2) Database Structure

Legacy SCADA databases contain multiple tables with sensor readings. Each table has a composite primary key structure:

  • REMOTA: Remote station identifier
  • IDENTIFICADOR: Sensor/device identifier within the station
  • TIPO_INFORMACION: Information type code (0, 1, 2...)
  • FECHA: Timestamp of the reading
  • VALOR: Measured value

Example table: Historico_Caudalimetros

REMOTA | IDENTIFICADOR | TIPO_INFORMACION | FECHA                   | VALOR
-------+---------------+------------------+-------------------------+-------
109    | 1             | 0                | 2025-11-12 12:00:09.000 | 0
109    | 1             | 1                | 2025-11-12 12:00:09.000 | 0
109    | 2             | 0                | 2025-11-12 12:00:09.000 | 125.5

3) Device Configuration

Each mdm.measurement.device requires:

  • Set remotecontrol_id to "SCADA Abaran"
  • No device-level remotecontrol_params needed

4) Sensor Configuration

Each mdm.measurement.device.sensor needs remotecontrol_params (JSON):

Required fields:

  • table: Table name (e.g., "Historico_Caudalimetros", "Historico_Presion")
  • remota: Remote station ID (REMOTA column value)
  • identificador: Sensor identifier (IDENTIFICADOR column value)
  • tipo_informacion: Information type code (TIPO_INFORMACION column value)

Optional fields:

  • start_date: Initial sync date (default: last reading or current year start)

Example sensor configuration:

{
  "table": "Historico_Caudalimetros",
  "remota": 109,
  "identificador": 1,
  "tipo_informacion": 0,
  "start_date": "2025-01-01"
}

Another example (pressure sensor):

{
  "table": "Historico_Presion",
  "remota": 109,
  "identificador": 5,
  "tipo_informacion": 1
}

5) SQL Query Example

For a sensor configured as above, the system generates:

SELECT VALOR, FECHA
FROM Historico_Caudalimetros
WHERE REMOTA = 109
  AND IDENTIFICADOR = 1
  AND TIPO_INFORMACION = 0
  AND FECHA >= '2025-01-01 00:00:00'
  AND FECHA <= '2025-11-12 23:59:59'
  AND VALOR IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY FECHA ASC

6) Export Sensors Catalog

Before configuring sensors, export the complete catalog from SCADA database:

  1. Execute action "SCADA Abaran: Export sensors catalog"
  2. Download CSV file from attachments
  3. Use REMOTA, IDENTIFICADOR, TIPO_INFORMACION values to configure sensors in Odoo

The CSV joins tables ELEMENTOS_INSTALACION and INFORMACION_HIDRAULICA to show:

  • Identification: REMOTA, TIPO_ELEMENTO, IDENTIFICADOR, TIPO_INFORMACION
  • Device info: DEVICE_NAME, DEVICE_DESCRIPTION (from ELEMENTOS_INSTALACION)
  • Sensor info: SENSOR_NAME (from INFORMACION_HIDRAULICA.DESCRIPCION_INFORMACION)

Only shows sensors where HISTORICOS = 1 (have historical data available).

7) Execution

Run the procedure "SCADA Abaran: Daily Sync" to import readings from all configured sensors.

8) Available Historical Tables

  • HISTORICO_ASPIRACIONES
  • HISTORICO_BALSAS
  • HISTORICO_BOMBAS
  • HISTORICO_CAUDALIMETROS
  • HISTORICO_CORRIENTE
  • HISTORICO_ENERGIA_ACTIVA
  • HISTORICO_ENERGIA_REACTIVA
  • HISTORICO_FACTOR_POTENCIA
  • HISTORICO_POTENCIA_ACTIVA
  • HISTORICO_POTENCIA_REACTIVA
  • HISTORICO_TEMPERATURA
  • HISTORICO_TRANSMISORES_PRESION
  • HISTORICO_VALVULAS

Note: All tables follow the same structure with composite key (REMOTA, IDENTIFICADOR, TIPO_INFORMACION, FECHA, VALOR)

9) Technical Features

  • Composite Primary Key: Handles 3-field keys (REMOTA, IDENTIFICADOR, TIPO_INFORMACION)
  • Timezone Conversion: Automatic Europe/Madrid → UTC conversion
  • Millisecond Handling: Processes SQL Server datetime format with .000 milliseconds
  • UTF-8 Encoding: Correctly handles Spanish characters (ñ, á, é, í, ó, ú)
  • CSV Export: Generates sensor catalog from SCADA database tables
  • Audit Trail: Creates JSON attachments with detailed import results

10) Troubleshooting

  • Connection refused → Check host/port/firewall/VPN
  • Login failed → Verify credentials and database name
  • Driver not found → Install FreeTDS or SQL Server ODBC driver
  • No data returned → Verify REMOTA, IDENTIFICADOR, TIPO_INFORMACION values using exported CSV catalog
  • Wrong TDS version → Try different tds_version values (7.0, 7.1, 7.2, 7.3, 7.4, 8.0)
  • Encoding errors → UTF-8 encoding is automatically configured for SQL Server drivers
  • Empty CSV export → Check that ELEMENTOS_INSTALACION and INFORMACION_HIDRAULICA tables exist and have HISTORICOS=1 records

# Export sensors catalog from SCADA database to CSV # Joins ELEMENTOS_INSTALACION with INFORMACION_HIDRAULICA import csv from io import BytesIO Remote = self.remote_id # Connect to SQL Server (using context functions) cursor = sql_connect() bag['_sql_cursor'] = cursor try: # Query to join both tables query = """ SELECT e.REMOTA, e.TIPO_ELEMENTO, e.IDENTIFICADOR, e.NOMBRE as device_name, e.DESCRIPCION as device_description, e.HISTORICOS, i.TIPO_INFORMACION, i.DESCRIPCION_INFORMACION as sensor_name FROM ELEMENTOS_INSTALACION e INNER JOIN INFORMACION_HIDRAULICA i ON e.REMOTA = i.REMOTA AND e.TIPO_ELEMENTO = i.TIPO_ELEMENTO AND e.IDENTIFICADOR = i.IDENTIFICADOR WHERE e.HISTORICOS = 1 ORDER BY e.REMOTA, e.TIPO_ELEMENTO, e.IDENTIFICADOR, i.TIPO_INFORMACION """ sql_execute(cursor, query, ()) rows = sql_fetchall(cursor) # Create CSV in memory (Python 2.7 compatible with BytesIO) output = BytesIO() writer = csv.writer(output, delimiter=';', quoting=csv.QUOTE_MINIMAL) # Write header writer.writerow([ 'REMOTA', 'TIPO_ELEMENTO', 'IDENTIFICADOR', 'TIPO_INFORMACION', 'DEVICE_NAME', 'DEVICE_DESCRIPTION', 'SENSOR_NAME' ]) # Write data rows (pyodbc now returns UTF-8 strings directly) for row in rows: scada_remote = row[0] element_type = row[1] identifier = row[2] device_name = row[3] or '' device_description = row[4] or '' history = row[5] info_type = row[6] sensor_name = row[7] or '' writer.writerow([ scada_remote, element_type, identifier, info_type, device_name, device_description, sensor_name ]) # Get CSV content as bytes csv_bytes = output.getvalue() output.close() # Create attachment attachment = env['ir.attachment'].create({ 'name': 'scada_abaran_sensors_catalog_%s.csv' % fields.Datetime.now().replace(' ', '_').replace(':', '-'), 'datas': base64.b64encode(csv_bytes), 'datas_fname': 'scada_abaran_sensors_catalog.csv', 'res_model': 'remotecontrol', 'res_id': Remote.id, 'type': 'binary', }) result = "Exported %d sensor records to CSV: %s" % (len(rows), attachment.name) finally: # Always close the connection cursor = bag.get('_sql_cursor') if cursor: sql_close(cursor) bag['result'] = result

# Build sensors plan from sensor remotecontrol_params Remote = self.remote_id Sensor = env['mdm.measurement.device.sensor'] Reading = env['mdm.measurement.device.sensor.reading'] today_str = fields.Date.today() # Get all sensors with remotecontrol_params configured for THIS remote control sensors = Sensor.search([ ('remotecontrol_params', '!=', False), ('device_id.remotecontrol_id', '=', Remote.id) ]) # Build map of sensor_id -> most recent reading (single query optimization) last_readings_map = {} if sensors: sensor_ids = [s.id for s in sensors] cr = env.cr cr.execute( 'SELECT DISTINCT ON (sensor_id) sensor_id, measurement_time ' 'FROM mdm_measurement_device_sensor_reading ' 'WHERE sensor_id IN %s AND active = TRUE ' 'ORDER BY sensor_id, measurement_time DESC', (tuple(sensor_ids),) ) for row in cr.fetchall(): last_readings_map[row[0]] = row[1] # Build execution plan plan = [] for sensor in sensors: device = sensor.device_id # Parse sensor configuration try: sensor_cfg = json.loads(sensor.remotecontrol_params or '{}') or {} except Exception: sensor_cfg = {} # Get configuration from sensor table_name = sensor_cfg.get('table') remota = sensor_cfg.get('remota') identificador = sensor_cfg.get('identificador') tipo_informacion = sensor_cfg.get('tipo_informacion') # Validate required parameters if not table_name or remota is None or identificador is None or tipo_informacion is None: continue # Determine initial date for this sensor last_reading_time = last_readings_map.get(sensor.id) if last_reading_time: try: initial_date = fields.Date.to_string( fields.Datetime.from_string(last_reading_time) + timedelta(days=1)) except Exception: initial_date = str(last_reading_time)[:10] else: # Use start_date from sensor config or Jan 1 of current year start_cfg = sensor_cfg.get('start_date') if start_cfg: initial_date = start_cfg[:10] else: year_str = today_str[:4] initial_date = '%s-01-01' % year_str plan.append({ 'sensor_id': sensor.id, 'device_id': device.id, 'table': table_name, 'remota': remota, 'identificador': identificador, 'tipo_informacion': tipo_informacion, 'initial_date': initial_date, }) bag['sensors_plan'] = plan bag['plan_count'] = len(plan)

# Fetch readings from SCADA Abaran SQL database and upsert into Odoo Remote = self.remote_id SensorModel = env['mdm.measurement.device.sensor'] plan = bag.get('sensors_plan') or [] if not plan: raise Exception("No sensors in plan. Run 'Get devices (plan)' first.") final_date = fields.Date.today() initial_date = None total_upserts = 0 total_errors = 0 items = [] # Connect to SCADA database and store cursor in bag cursor = sql_connect() bag['_sql_cursor'] = cursor try: for sensor_plan in plan: sensor_id = sensor_plan['sensor_id'] device_id = sensor_plan['device_id'] table_name = sensor_plan['table'] remota = sensor_plan['remota'] identificador = sensor_plan['identificador'] tipo_informacion = sensor_plan['tipo_informacion'] initial_date = sensor_plan['initial_date'] sensor_record = SensorModel.browse(sensor_id) try: # Build query with composite primary key WHERE clause query = """ SELECT VALOR, FECHA FROM %s WHERE REMOTA = ? AND IDENTIFICADOR = ? AND TIPO_INFORMACION = ? AND FECHA >= ? AND FECHA <= ? AND VALOR IS NOT NULL ORDER BY FECHA ASC """ % table_name query_params = ( remota, identificador, tipo_informacion, initial_date + ' 00:00:00.000', final_date + ' 23:59:59.999' ) sql_execute(cursor, query, query_params) rows = sql_fetchall(cursor) upserts = 0 errs = 0 readings_summary = [] for row in rows: try: raw_value = float(row[0]) if row[0] is not None else 0.0 fecha_value = row[1] # Convert timestamp to Odoo format (UTC) # SCADA stores timestamps in Europe/Madrid timezone if hasattr(fecha_value, 'strftime'): # It's a datetime object from pyodbc (naive, assumed Europe/Madrid) local_tz = pytz.timezone('Europe/Madrid') # Make it timezone-aware as Madrid time local_dt = local_tz.localize(fecha_value) # Convert to UTC utc_dt = local_dt.astimezone(pytz.UTC) # Convert to Odoo string format timestamp = fields.Datetime.to_string(utc_dt.replace(tzinfo=None)) else: # It's a string like '2025-11-12 12:00:09.000' # Parse it as Europe/Madrid time from datetime import datetime local_tz = pytz.timezone('Europe/Madrid') # Handle SQL Server format with milliseconds fecha_str = str(fecha_value)[:19] naive_dt = datetime.strptime(fecha_str, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') local_dt = local_tz.localize(naive_dt) utc_dt = local_dt.astimezone(pytz.UTC) timestamp = fields.Datetime.to_string(utc_dt.replace(tzinfo=None)) # Upsert reading into Odoo Remote.upsert( 'mdm.measurement.device.sensor.reading', { 'sensor_id': sensor_record.id, 'measurement_time': timestamp }, { 'value': raw_value, 'remotecontrol_origin_id': Remote.id } ) upserts += 1 readings_summary.append({ 'time': timestamp, 'value': raw_value }) except Exception as e: errs += 1 readings_summary.append({ 'row': str(row), 'error': str(e) }) total_upserts += upserts total_errors += errs items.append({ 'sensor_id': sensor_id, 'device_id': device_id, 'table': table_name, 'remota': remota, 'identificador': identificador, 'tipo_informacion': tipo_informacion, 'status': 'success', 'points_found': len(rows), 'upserts': upserts, 'errors': errs, 'readings': readings_summary[:10] # Limit to first 10 for audit }) except Exception as e: total_errors += 1 items.append({ 'sensor_id': sensor_id, 'device_id': device_id, 'table': table_name, 'remota': remota, 'identificador': identificador, 'tipo_informacion': tipo_informacion, 'status': 'error', 'error': str(e) }) finally: # Always close the connection cursor = bag.get('_sql_cursor') if cursor: sql_close(cursor)
# Create audit attachment audit = { 'executed_at': str(fields.Datetime.now()), 'initial_date': initial_date if plan else None, 'final_date': final_date, 'total_upserts': total_upserts, 'total_errors': total_errors, 'sensors_processed': len(plan), 'items': items } try: audit_json = json.dumps(audit, ensure_ascii=True, indent=2, default=str) b64 = base64.b64encode(audit_json.encode('utf-8')) except Exception as json_error: simple_audit = { 'executed_at': str(fields.Datetime.now()), 'total_upserts': total_upserts, 'total_errors': total_errors, 'error': str(json_error) } audit_json = json.dumps(simple_audit, ensure_ascii=True, indent=2) b64 = base64.b64encode(audit_json.encode('utf-8')) fname = 'scada_abaran_readings_%s.json' % ( fields.Datetime.now().replace(':', '').replace('-', '').replace(' ', '_') ) att = env['ir.attachment'].create({ 'name': fname, 'datas_fname': fname, 'datas': b64, 'mimetype': 'application/json', 'res_model': 'remotecontrol', 'res_id': Remote.id }) Remote.message_post( body="[SCADA Abaran Readings] upserts=%s errors=%s sensors=%s" % ( total_upserts, total_errors, len(plan) ), attachment_ids=[att.id] ) bag['upserts'] = total_upserts bag['errors'] = total_errors bag['audit_attachment_id'] = att.id
